Ellingham diagrams show how the quantity ǻG for a reaction varies over a range of 
temperatures. 
 
The ǻG values for different reactions can be combined using Hess’s law. 
 
For a reaction to be able to occur, the overall value of ǻG must be less than zero. 
 
 
 
 
Using the Ellingham diagram shown, which one of the following statements is correct? 
 
 
 
A 
Nickel can reduce tin(IV) oxide at 300 °C. 
 
B 
Carbon can reduce chromium(III) oxide at 1500 °C forming carbon dioxide and chromium. 
 
C 
Chromium(III) oxide and nickel oxide will decompose to their elements at all the 
temperatures shown. 
 
D 
Chromium will react with steam at all the temperatures shown. 
 
E 
Nickel oxide can be reduced by carbon at 300 °C forming carbon monoxide and nickel.
